question: How do you monitor, profile, debug and tune a large LLM inference cluster, from GPU counters through batching, scheduling, quantization and application-level optimizations?
contributions: Application-level optimizations: prompt compression, prefix caching, cascading, streaming

limits: Authors and year are not printed in the extracted text.
Chapter states numeric values in its metrics tables are illustrative; actual benchmarks are in an external GitHub repository.
Most numbers are rules of thumb or hypothetical examples, with no named model, dataset or hardware measurement.
Mentions of vLLM, NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, NVL72 features reflect 2025 software and may date.
Claims like ChatGPT using model cascading are stated as 'widely believed', not shown.
practices: Run an observe, hypothesize, tune, verify loop and canary-roll every optimization to a small traffic slice first (Profiling, Debugging, and Tuning Inference Performance).
Track cache hit versus miss counts for prefix, prompt-embedding and KV caches (e.g. vllm:gpu_prefix_cache_hits over queries) and check tokenizer differences first when prefix matching fails.
Use Prometheus/Grafana with DCGM for GPU metrics, add application counters (batch size changes, NCCL errors) and overlay them with RPS and latency (Monitoring System Metrics).
Prefer Nsight Compute PC sampling first on live servers, and use Nsight Systems with NVTX ranges for prefill/decode/stream timelines (Profiling with Nsight).
Use lightweight metric-based thresholds in production (Table 16-1) rather than continuous heavy profilers.
Set a MoE capacity factor of 1.2-1.5 so overloaded experts spill to a replica (Monitoring System Metrics).
Cap the dynamic batching delay well under the p99 SLO and plot latency percentiles against load to find the inflection point (Dynamic Batching).
Choose batch size at the throughput-latency knee, about 90% of peak throughput, and watch p95/p99 not only p50 (Maximizing GPU Utilization).
Prefer continuous batching for chat; consider a hybrid of short timer plus max batch size for a custom scheduler (Continuous Batching, Continuous Scheduling).
Use chunked prefill to smooth latency, knowing it does not reduce total attention work (Table 16-5).
Use latency-aware length-balanced batches rather than FIFO (Tables 16-6, 16-7).
Overlap compute and communication with multiple CUDA streams, pinned memory, events and NCCL groups; verify with profiling (Overlapping Communication and Computation).
Monitor power and thermal throttling with DCGM and nvidia-smi; consider a boost-off flag or clock caps (Power and Thermal Constraints).
Fail fast, apply backpressure and keep at least 10-15% idle buffer replicas, 100% for critical services (Error Handling).
Keep weights in HBM, use paged KV cache with offload for rarely used entries, and consider KV quantization (Memory).
Start with 8-bit weights, then 4-bit weight-only (GPTQ/AWQ), then W4A8 only if needed; calibrate on workload-like data and A/B test downstream quality (Quantization).
Fuse quantize-dequantize into compute kernels (Fusing Quantization-Dequantization).
Enable prefix caching, size the cache to measured hit rate, use radix-tree prefix cache with LRU eviction (Prefix Caching).
Summarize oldest 25% of messages when a conversation exceeds 75% of max context, and verify the compressed prompt retains key facts (Prompt Compression).
Cascade to smaller models using a light classifier or confidence, log which model handled each request, and retrain the router periodically (Model Cascading).
Stream tokens in batches of 2-5, use a bounded buffer of about 50-100 tokens, TCP_NODELAY, and allow user interrupts (Streaming Responses).
Set server-side output limits (e.g. 4,096 tokens) and timeouts (e.g. 30 s) (Token Output Limits and Timeouts).

terms.definition: a specialization of request batching that assembles batches of incoming inference requests of dynamic sizes on the fly
also known as in-flight batching or iteration-level scheduling; refills batches on every token-generation iteration rather than waiting for complete sequences to finish
treats the GPU like an OS scheduler treats a CPU; launches independent small decode kernels on separate CUDA streams
splitting long prompts into chunks and interleaving prefill and decode work
useful GPU utilization, hardware doing useful work
compute the KV for a shared prefix once and reuse it for subsequent requests; also called prefix memoization
choosing the right model per request via tiered deployment; also fallback model routing
a separate scale for each fixed-size block, typically 32 elements, within a tensor
intentionally delaying token sends to smooth streaming rate, e.g. 50 ms between sends
